review_comment: The eval() call constructs and executes Python code using untrusted network message data without validation, enabling arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability is introduced by directly using empty string keys from the data dictionary to build class names. Replace eval() with a mapping dictionary or allowlist of permitted class names to prevent code injection.

The code passes raw compressed message data directly to constructObject, bypassing the message type validation performed on the unpacked dictionary. This could allow malicious type strings to reach the eval() function in constructObject. Pass the validated unpacked dictionary (tmp) to constructObject instead of the raw data to ensure type validation occurs before unsafe deserialization operations.

The code dynamically constructs objects using untrusted input that controls both class selection and constructor arguments. This enables injection of arbitrary objects whose process() methods will be executed. Implement an allowlist of permitted message types and validate data structure before object construction to prevent unauthorized class instantiation.
